response.query: Which author disambiguation algorithms and feature sets (ORCID, affiliation, email, coauthor graph, embeddings) minimize error rates in bibliometric datasets?
response.answer: Algorithms combining ORCID, affiliation, co-author graph, and embeddings minimize error rates in bibliometric datasets. Feature sets like these improve disambiguation accuracy. Recent studies show best results with these combined features.

results.title: Author name disambiguation literature review with ...
results.content: This article presents an author name disambiguation (AND) literature review using the theory of the consolidated meta-analytic approach, including quantitative techniques and bibliometric aspects. The data presentation and interrelation using the consolidated meta-analytic approach of TEMAC allows for a review of the most relevant authors and citations, journals, countries, organizations, or universities, and knowledge areas most related to the research field. Using the document titles and abstracts in the WoS and Scopus merged databases, we generate a word cloud as shown in Fig. 7.The cloud included words related to the AND problem and solving approaches, such as data, clustering, information, learning, similarity, publication, model network, libraries, and graph. This work is classified according to the taxonomy in the type of approach as Author Assignment and explored evidence as Citation Information and Web Information (i.e., data extracted from DBLP and BDBComp). Based on the co-citation analysis performed across the studied time-space (2003–2022), the works present mainly the use of author grouping approaches.
